insights.headline: China's central bank bought gold for a 23rd straight month as ETF inflows hit records and the Fed stayed hawkish
points: PBOC's September gold purchase of ~740,000 oz was its biggest since March; holdings now 77.47 million oz — a 23rd straight month of buying.
Fed Governor Waller said further rate hikes remain likely; gold closed at $4,196.07, up 1.5% on the day, below its 50-day average of $4,346.27.
Peter Brandt flagged a weekly head-and-shoulders pattern warning toward $2,890 if $4,100–$4,200 breaks, stressing it is not a forecast.
COMEX silver ended the week 1.16% higher at $60.670, snapping a two-week losing streak.
India's gold demand stayed sluggish as prices rebounded; dealer discounts narrowed to $6 an ounce.
insights.summary: China's central bank added roughly 740,000 ounces of gold in September — its biggest monthly purchase since March — taking holdings to 77.47 million ounces for a 23rd consecutive month of buying, even as the price fall cut the reported reserve value to $323.52 billion. Gold ETFs drew a record $31 billion in the third quarter, yet Fed Governor Waller's warning that further hikes remain likely kept the metal pinned near $4,200. In India, MCX gold futures held around Rs 1.51 lakh per 10 grams while buyers stayed price-sensitive ahead of the festive season.

items.summary: China's central bank added roughly 740,000 ounces of gold to its reserves in September — the biggest monthly purchase since March — extending its buying streak to a 23rd consecutive month and taking holdings to 77.47 million ounces, Reuters reports. September's 6%-plus price fall cut the reported value of those reserves to $323.52 billion from $350.08 billion a month earlier.
items.title: China's central bank buys gold for 23rd straight month as September pace hits fastest since March

items.summary: Gold has dropped about 26% from its January peak near $5,595 an ounce, Mint writes, weighed down by US 10-year yields around 5.27%, a stronger dollar, oil-driven inflation worries and profit-taking. Mirae Asset MF expects central-bank demand near 700 tonnes in 2026, and India's upcoming festive season could lend support.
items.title: Will gold prices fall further? Check reasons behind the recent dip, forecasts and more

items.summary: Domestic gold buying has picked up after the recent price correction, but shoppers are prioritising affordability — trading down to lighter pieces rather than stepping away, per the Economic Times.
items.title: Gold buying picks up after price correction, but shoppers prioritise affordability

items.summary: Gold closed at $4,196.07, up 1.5% on the day, even as Fed Governor Christopher Waller warned further rate hikes remain likely, keeping a cap on the rally. World Gold Council data showed gold ETFs drew $10 billion in September, lifting holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes, and Morgan Stanley's Amy Gower expects $4,000 to hold as support with a return above $5,000 in the second half of 2027.
items.title: Gold's record ETF inflows collide with Waller's rate warning

items.summary: Veteran trader Peter Brandt has flagged a head-and-shoulders pattern on gold's weekly chart, warning the metal could slide toward $2,890 if support at $4,100–$4,200 breaks. He stressed the chart is not a forecast, and noted continued Chinese central-bank buying could underpin prices.
items.title: Veteran trader Peter Brandt warns gold could slide toward $2,890 on weekly head-and-shoulders

items.summary: Front-month COMEX silver gained 1.16% on the week to $60.670, snapping a two-week losing streak, per Dow Jones Market Data via Morningstar.
items.title: COMEX silver ends the week 1.16% higher at $60.670, snapping a two-week losing streak

items.summary: Gold futures on the MCX climbed toward Rs 1.51 lakh per 10 grams as firm spot demand supported prices.
items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.51 lakh/10 gm on firm spot demand

items.summary: Indian gold demand stayed sluggish this week as prices rebounded, Reuters reports via The Hindu BusinessLine, with dealer discounts narrowing to $6 an ounce over official domestic prices.
items.title: Indian gold demand sluggish as prices rebound; discounts narrow to $6 an ounce

items.summary: India's foreign-exchange reserves fell $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in the week ended October 2, RBI data shows, per Devdiscourse.
items.title: India's forex reserves fall $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in week ended Oct 2

items.summary: PN Gadgil Jewellers posted a 22.4% jump in second-quarter revenue, riding festive-season jewellery demand, CNBC-TV18 reports.
items.title: PN Gadgil Jewellers Q2 revenue jumps 22.4% on festive demand

trending.summary: The PBOC extended its buying streak to 23 months with its largest purchase since March, buying September's dip. Steady official demand is a key floor under bullion, per Morgan Stanley.
trending.title: Central banks keep stacking gold

trending.summary: Record third-quarter gold ETF inflows of $31bn collided with Waller's warning that more rate hikes remain likely. Wednesday's US CPI report is the next tie-breaker for the December hike debate.
trending.title: Fed hawkishness vs record ETF demand

trending.summary: MCX gold held near Rs 1.51 lakh per 10g while physical demand lagged the rebound and discounts narrowed to $6/oz. Jewellers are pushing festive offers as Navratri–Diwali buying begins.
